climate.overview_html: IPCC-65 enters its fourth day in Addis Ababa with the AR7 delivery-timeline still unresolved across six consecutive plenary sessions — a decision is due by Friday, 16 October; Chair Jim Skea has expressed confidence in a “constructive result” before the session closes. The COP31 Host Country Agreement with Türkiye formally entered into force on 9 October, locking in the Antalya EXPO Center for the 9–20 November summit. Ahead of COP31, the CVF–V20 and VCMI jointly released a Paris Agreement Article 6 carbon-market handbook for climate-vulnerable nations on 14 October, and the UNFCCC separately opened the UN carbon market under Article 6.4 to clean cooking projects — while the EU set its COP31 negotiating position, prioritising a binding “35 by 35” clean-electrification goal.

items.source: IPCC Secretariat / Carbon Brief / Earth Negotiations Bulletin
items.headline: IPCC-65 Day 4 in Addis Ababa: AR7 Timeline Decision Due Friday 16 Oct; Six Consecutive Plenaries Without Agreement; Chair Skea Confident of “Constructive Result”
items.summary: IPCC-65, running October 12–16 at the UN Economic Commission for Africa in Addis Ababa, entered its fourth day on October 15 with the AR7 delivery-timeline unresolved across six consecutive plenaries. The core divide: the EU and small island states want all three Working Group reports completed before the second Global Stocktake (~2028); a bloc including India seeks WG2 and WG3 deferred to 2029. IPCC Chair Jim Skea, who has proposed approving all three reports by September 2028, expressed confidence a constructive result is achievable before the session closes October 16. The COP31 co-presidency (Turkey/Australia) held a virtual consultation with IPCC delegates on October 14. WWF and major scientific organisations have called this session 'perhaps the last chance' to align all three reports with the 2028 Stocktake deadline.

items.headline: COP31 Host Country Agreement with Türkiye Formally Enters into Force; Antalya EXPO Center Confirmed for 9–20 November 2026 Summit
items.summary: The COP31 Host Country Agreement between the UNFCCC Secretariat and the Republic of Türkiye formally entered into force on October 9, 2026, confirming the Antalya EXPO Center as the conference venue for the 31st Conference of the Parties, November 9–20. Turkey's Environment and Urbanisation Minister Murat Kurum, serving as COP31 President, has signalled that carbon markets will take a 'rightful place' at the summit. Key unresolved pre-COP31 issues include 1.5°C overshoot language, fossil fuel phase-out commitments, and finalising the New Collective Quantified Goal on climate finance.

items.headline: CVF–V20 and VCMI Release Paris Agreement Article 6 Handbook for Climate-Vulnerable Nations Ahead of COP31; Focus on Carbon-Market Engagement, Corresponding Adjustments and Host-Country Safeguards
items.summary: The Climate Vulnerable Forum–Vulnerable Twenty Group of Finance Ministers (CVF-V20) and the Voluntary Carbon Markets Integrity initiative (VCMI) jointly released a practical handbook on Paris Agreement Article 6 on October 14, designed to help climate-vulnerable nations navigate the emerging carbon market framework ahead of COP31. The handbook covers Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs), corresponding adjustments, and safeguards for host countries participating in Article 6.2 bilateral deals and the Article 6.4 UN-supervised mechanism. It also addresses how vulnerable nations can leverage these instruments to attract climate finance while protecting their nationally determined contributions.

items.headline: UNFCCC Article 6.4 Supervisory Body Opens UN Carbon Market to Clean Cooking Projects; Expands Access to Carbon Finance for Cookstove Programmes in Developing Nations
items.summary: The UNFCCC Supervisory Body for the Article 6.4 mechanism announced on October 9 that clean cooking projects are now eligible to generate carbon credits under the UN-supervised carbon market. The decision expands carbon finance pathways for projects replacing solid-fuel cookstoves in developing countries — a sector representing significant health and emissions co-benefits. Cookstove replacement projects address approximately 1.9 million premature deaths annually from indoor air pollution while delivering measurable Scope 1 and Scope 2 emission reductions. The move comes ahead of COP31, where carbon markets are expected to be a central negotiating topic.

items.headline: European Union Sets COP31 Negotiating Position: Priority on “35 by 35” Clean Electrification Goal; France Seeks Binding Decision; EU Maintains 1.5°C Ambition Framing
items.summary: The European Union has formalised its COP31 negotiating position, identifying clean electrification as a top priority. France is leading a push for a binding COP31 decision on the '35 by 35' goal — raising electricity's share of global final energy to 35% by 2035. The EU also supports maintaining the 1.5°C ambition framing in the cover decision, and wants substantial progress on the New Collective Quantified Goal for climate finance. Turkey, as COP31 host-president, has framed the summit as an 'implementation COP' focused on delivering on existing commitments rather than announcing new targets.

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Trudy (Eastern Pacific) — Rapidly Intensifying, Mexico Landfall Threat
major_events.status: As of 15 Oct: ~70 mph (~60 kt), approximately 315 miles south of Acapulco, moving WNW at ~8 mph; NHC forecasts hurricane status by overnight 15/16 Oct, major hurricane (Cat 3+, 130–140 mph) by Friday 17 Oct; expected landfall near Manzanillo, Colima/Jalisco coast, late Saturday–Sunday (17–19 Oct); NHC cautions track is “more uncertain than usual” due to interaction with remnant circulation of Hurricane Simon
major_events.impact: Coastal watches for SW and W-central Mexico coasts expected Wednesday–Thursday; compound flooding and landslide hazard is elevated because Simon’s prior rainfall has already saturated soils along the Guerrero–Colima corridor; major hurricane landfall possible in a region still recovering from Simon

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Haze / Indonesian Peatland Wildfires (Day 17+)
major_events.status: Singapore hit its highest haze category on 14 Oct (1-hour PM2.5: 288 μg/m³ in western districts — “very high” threshold); East Timor closed schools as a health precaution; Indonesia resisting national disaster declaration despite hundreds of thousands of hectares burned in Borneo and Sumatra; Indonesia’s worst wildfire-haze crisis since 2015
major_events.impact: Tens of thousands treated for respiratory illness across Central Kalimantan, South Sumatra and Papua; >1,600 domestic flights disrupted; dense smog grounding aerial water-bombing and cloud-seeding operations; Singapore has reinstated haze-related medical subsidies last used in 2015

weather.overview_html: Tropical Storm Trudy intensified overnight to approximately 70 mph and is on track to become a major hurricane (Cat 3–4) by Friday, threatening Mexico’s Colima–Jalisco coast with potential landfall Saturday or Sunday; the track remains uncertain due to interaction with Hurricane Simon’s remnants. In Southeast Asia, Singapore hit its highest haze category on 14 October (PM2.5: 288 μg/m³) — the worst wildfire-haze crisis since 2015, with more than 1,600 flights disrupted and tens of thousands seeking respiratory treatment. In the US, Hurricane Isaias left four dead and nearly 900,000 without power after making Category 2 landfall near Destin, Florida on 10 October, with cleanup and power restoration still ongoing across the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama.

items.source: NHC / UPI / Yahoo Weather / Fox Weather
items.headline: Tropical Storm Trudy Rapidly Intensifies to ~70 mph (15 Oct); NHC Forecasts Major Hurricane by Friday, Landfall Near Manzanillo, Colima, Saturday–Sunday; Watches Expected by Wednesday–Thursday; Track Uncertainty Elevated by Simon Remnants
items.summary: As of the NHC's October 15 advisory, Tropical Storm Trudy had sustained winds of approximately 70 mph and was located about 315 miles south of Acapulco, moving west-northwest at ~8 mph — an intensification of 25 mph since the morning advisory. The NHC forecasts Trudy to reach hurricane intensity overnight and become a major hurricane (Category 3 or higher, potentially 130–140 mph) by Friday October 17, with a likely landfall near Manzanillo, Colima, over the weekend (October 17–19). The NHC has cautioned the track is 'more uncertain than usual' because both Trudy and the remnant circulation of Hurricane Simon are active near each other, creating complex steering dynamics. Coastal watches for southwestern and west-central Mexico are expected by late Wednesday or Thursday. Compound flooding and landslide risk is significantly elevated: Simon's earlier rainfall has saturated soils from Guerrero to Colima, meaning Trudy's rains will trigger runoff and slides faster than typical.

items.headline: SE Asian Haze Escalates: Singapore Hits Highest Haze Category (1-hr PM2.5: 288 μg/m³, 14 Oct) — Worst Since 2015; East Timor Schools Closed; >1,600 Flights Disrupted; Indonesia Rejects National Disaster Status
items.summary: Singapore recorded a 1-hour PM2.5 reading of 288 μg/m³ in western districts on October 14 — its highest haze category ('very high', threshold >251 μg/m³), a level not reached since the 2015 crisis. Singapore reinstated government-subsidised haze-related medical treatment, a measure last used in 2015. East Timor ordered school closures as a health precaution. Indonesia's wildfires have burned hundreds of thousands of hectares in Borneo and Sumatra, described by ExpatGo as the worst wildfire-haze crisis in 11 years. Indonesia is resisting declaring a national disaster despite the scale of damage. More than 1,600 domestic flights have been disrupted, and dense smog continues to prevent aerial water-bombing and cloud-seeding operations in Central Kalimantan. Tens of thousands have sought treatment for respiratory illness across Central Kalimantan, South Sumatra and Papua. A late rainy season driven by El Niño means the fires could persist through October–November.

items.headline: Hurricane Isaias (Category 2, 105 mph) Makes Gulf Coast Landfall Near Destin, Florida; 4 Dead; Peak ~900,000 Without Power; Cleanup Ongoing Across Florida Panhandle and Southern Alabama
items.summary: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, at approximately 8:30 p.m. CDT on October 10, 2026, with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (Category 2). At least four people were killed — two in Florida's Escambia County and two in Alabama. Wind gusts above 100 mph were measured at six landfall-area stations. Peak power outages reached approximately 900,000 customers across the Gulf Coast, dropping to around 390,000 by Sunday October 12 as crews from neighboring states provided mutual-aid restoration. Tornadoes were reported as far inland as South Carolina and North Carolina. Boil-water notices remained in effect across parts of the Florida Panhandle as of October 14–15. The storm's remnants are no longer active, but debris clearing, power restoration and water-system repairs continue.

renewables.overview_html: China’s National Energy Administration confirmed installed renewable capacity reached 2.496 TW by end-August 2026 — 60.8% of the country’s total power capacity — as the country targets 3.5 TW by 2030. In the US, the Trump administration’s Interior Department filed to rescind the operating approval for the nearly complete 704 MW Revolution Wind offshore project — the third attempt to halt a project already delivering electricity to New England. In Europe, Germany’s PNE AG cut its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance by ~40% due to wind-project delays and permitting backlogs; and Finland’s Fingrid published mandatory grid-forming requirements for large new wind and solar plants in converter-dominated portions of its grid.

items.headline: China Renewable Capacity Reaches 2.496 TW by End-August 2026 (60.8% of Total Power Capacity); Solar 1.274 TW, Wind 679 GW; NEA Targets 3.5 TW by 2030
items.summary: China's National Energy Administration (NEA) announced on October 14 that installed renewable power capacity reached 2.496 TW by the end of August 2026, accounting for 60.8% of the country's total power capacity. Solar reached 1.274 TW, wind 679 GW, and hydropower 454 GW. The figure marks a substantial year-on-year increase from 2.34 TW at end-2025 and positions China well toward its 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) target of 3.5 TW of renewable capacity. The pace of additions — particularly utility-scale and distributed solar — means the 3.5 TW target is likely to be exceeded ahead of schedule.

items.headline: Trump Administration Seeks Federal Court Permission to Rescind Revolution Wind’s Operating Approval; Project ~80% Complete and Already Delivering Power; Third Attempt to Halt the 704 MW Project
items.summary: The US Department of the Interior filed in federal court on October 13 seeking permission to rescind the three-year-old federal operating approval for Revolution Wind, a 704 MW offshore wind farm off the coasts of Connecticut and Rhode Island. The project has already begun delivering electricity to New England and completed most construction by September 2026. Two prior stop-work orders — issued in 2025 — were overturned by courts, which ordered construction to resume. Interior did not detail its legal basis for the rescission request, but the Trump administration's broader offshore wind rollback has included pausing five federal leases. Revolution Wind is described as capable of reaching full 704 MW output by end-2026.

items.headline: PNE AG Cuts 2026 Adjusted EBITDA Guidance ~40% (New Range: €65–80 M vs. Prior €110–140 M); Wind Project Sale Delays and Permitting Backlogs Cited; Some 2026 Revenue Shifts to 2027
items.summary: German SDax-listed wind park developer PNE AG issued a significant earnings guidance cut on October 14, reducing its 2026 adjusted EBITDA forecast to €65–80 million from the prior range of €110–140 million — a reduction of approximately 40% at midpoint. The company cited delays in planned wind park project sales, delayed permitting approvals, and a strategic decision to retain some operating wind parks rather than sell them. Revenue once expected in 2026 will now shift into 2027. The guidance cut reflects the continuing difficulty of the German wind development market, where approval procedures have lengthened significantly despite recent regulatory reform efforts.

items.headline: Fingrid (Finland) Mandates Grid-Forming Capability for New Large-Scale Wind and Solar Plants in Converter-Dominated Grid Regions; Requirements Published 15 October 2026
items.summary: Finnish transmission system operator Fingrid published mandatory technical requirements on October 15 obliging new large-scale wind and solar plants connected in converter-dominated portions of its network to provide grid-forming control. The requirements respond to a growing stability risk: converter-connected generation was feeding roughly 65% of Finland's system power at peak times in 2026. Grid-following inverters, which dominate current renewable installations, require the presence of synchronous generation to maintain stable voltage and frequency; without grid-forming capability, adding more converter-based capacity in weak grid areas risks instability. Fingrid already operates synchronous condensers and a STATCOM to provide synthetic inertia; the new requirements shift the cost and responsibility to project developers. Finland had approximately 8,885 MW of installed wind and ~1,500 MW of solar as of mid-2026.

science.overview_html: The standout publication of the period is a Microsoft Research-led paper in Nature (14 October) introducing Probabilistic Bias Correction (PBC) for subseasonal-to-seasonal forecasting: applied to ECMWF’s AI and dynamical models, PBC roughly doubled the raw subseasonal skill of the AI Forecasting System and tripled precipitation skill across all six major operational centres, whose debiased models had previously shown negative precipitation skill at S2S timescales. The MicroDuet system combining PBC with a transformer ensemble model placed first in the inaugural AI Weather Quest competition. MIT News covered the work the same day, highlighting the 2–6 week window as the critical gap for agricultural planning and disaster preparedness. In applied climate science, the Climate Impact Lab estimates the 2026 Super El Niño could drive up to ~500,000 excess heat-related deaths globally, with the heaviest toll projected in tropical and subtropical lower-income nations.

items.headline: Microsoft Research & Nature: “Advancing Subseasonal Forecasting with Machine Learning” — Probabilistic Bias Correction (PBC) Doubles AI-Model S2S Skill, MicroDuet Wins AI Weather Quest; All Six Operational Centres Show Negative Precipitation Skill Without Correction
items.meta: Microsoft Research et al. · Nature, published 14 October 2026
items.summary: A Microsoft Research-led team published 'Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning' in Nature on October 14. The paper introduces Probabilistic Bias Correction (PBC), a machine-learning framework that learns to correct systematic errors in probabilistic subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) forecast ensembles using historical model output. Key results: (1) PBC applied to ECMWF's AI Forecasting System (AIFS-SUBS) doubled its raw subseasonal skill; (2) PBC applied to the operationally debiased ECMWF dynamical model improved skill for 91% of pressure, 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets; (3) all six major operational forecasting centres' debiased models showed negative skill for precipitation at S2S timescales — meaning they were performing worse than climatological averages — with PBC correcting this. The team's MicroDuet system (PBC + PoET transformer ensemble) placed first for all weather variables and lead times in the September–November inaugural season of the AI Weather Quest competition. MIT News covered the study the same day, noting the 2–6 week window is critical for agricultural planning and pre-positioning disaster resources. Code is open source. arXiv preprint: 2604.16238.

items.headline: Climate Impact Lab: 2026 Super El Niño Heat Could Cause ~500,000 Excess Deaths Globally; Heaviest Toll in Lower-Income Tropical and Subtropical Nations; Health Systems Risk Overwhelm
items.summary: The Climate Impact Lab has projected that the 2026 Super El Niño, combined with the ongoing background warming trend, could drive approximately half a million excess heat-related deaths globally, according to NBC News reporting around October 8. The heaviest mortality burden is expected in tropical and subtropical lower-income countries, particularly in South and Southeast Asia, sub-Saharan Africa and parts of South America, where populations have lower adaptive capacity and less access to cooling infrastructure. The projection compounds concerns raised in a concurrent Lancet/Bristol paper about inadequate preparedness for the El Niño's compound health effects. With the Niño 3.4 anomaly at +3.34°C and projected to peak near +3.7°C in December 2026, this El Niño already exceeds the 2015–16 record and its health impacts are expected to persist into mid-2027.

items.headline: AI Weather Quest: MicroDuet (Microsoft Research + MIT) Wins First Season; Bias Correction Doubled European AI Model’s Subseasonal Skill; Only Entry to Significantly Outperform Operationally Debiased ECMWF Dynamical Model Across All Variables and Lead Times
items.summary: MicroDuet, the joint entry of Microsoft Research and MIT's forecasting team, won the inaugural September–November season of the AI Weather Quest — a public S2S forecasting competition. It placed first for all weather variables and all lead times, and was the only submission to significantly outperform the operationally debiased ECMWF dynamical model across the full range of variables and lead times across the first two competition seasons. Applied to ECMWF's AIFS-SUBS, the team's Probabilistic Bias Correction method roughly tripled precipitation skill relative to the raw AI model output — reversing the negative skill found in all six major operational forecast centres' debiased precipitation runs at S2S timescales. A second-ranked competitive team applied a similar debiasing approach to FuXi-S2S, which had previously reported skillful Madden–Julian Oscillation prediction out to 36 days. The AI Weather Quest is organised under WMO's S2S prediction project.

items.title: TWIA Forecasts US$2.05 Billion Reinsurance and Cat Bond Need for 2027, Proposes 18% Budget Reduction
items.body_html: The Texas Windstorm Insurance Association (TWIA) has forecast a US$2.05 billion reinsurance and catastrophe bond requirement for its 2027 programme, according to an Artemis.bm report dated 7 October. The forecast accompanies a proposed 18% budget reduction, reflecting both continued tightening of TWIA’s exposure management and shifting reinsurance market conditions. TWIA insures properties in the high-risk Gulf Coast counties of Texas that the private market will not cover; its reinsurance tower is one of the largest state wind-pool programmes in the US. The 2027 programme will be informed by updated vendor catastrophe model loss estimates and current ILS market pricing, which has seen a global cat bond market reach a record ~US$65.6 billion outstanding in mid-2026.

items.title: Wildfire-Exposed Catastrophe Bond Issuance Reaches US$5.183 Billion YTD in 2026, Approaching Full-Year Record; Insurers Transfer Record Climate-Linked Risk to Capital Markets
items.body_html: Wildfire-exposed catastrophe bond issuance has reached US$5.183 billion year-to-date in 2026, according to Artemis.bm, rapidly approaching the full-year record of US$5.55 billion set in 2025. The surge reflects insurers and reinsurers accelerating their use of the capital markets to transfer wildfire risk, driven by escalating insured losses across California, the Mountain West and Southern Europe. The broader ILS market hit a record outstanding of approximately US$65.6 billion in mid-2026. The growth trajectory for wildfire-linked paper aligns with vendor model updates from Verisk and Moody’s that now incorporate climate-adjusted hazard frequencies and changing fire behaviour, raising modelled annual expected losses for wildfire perils.

items.title: MN8 Energy to Acquire Greenbacker Renewable Energy for US$375 Million; Combined 6 GW US Platform Expected to Close Q4 2026
items.body_html: MN8 Energy agreed on 28 July to acquire Greenbacker Renewable Energy Company LLC in a cash-and-equity deal valued at up to US$375 million (US$350 M upfront plus up to US$25 M in performance payments), pending Greenbacker shareholder approval, MN8 member approval and regulatory clearance — all expected in Q4 2026. The transaction combines MN8’s 4.3 GW portfolio across 29 US states with Greenbacker’s ~1.9 GW fleet in 22 states, creating a 6 GW-plus American independent power platform. Strategic driver: surging electricity demand from data centres and AI. The deal expands MN8’s presence in the Midwest and Northeast and adds wind, battery storage and distributed generation to its technology mix. CEO Jon Yoder will lead the combined company.
items.source_html: PV Tech / pv magazine USA

items.title: Trump Administration Files Federal Court Motion to Rescind Revolution Wind’s Operating Approval; Third Attempt to Halt 704 MW Near-Complete Offshore Project
items.body_html: Interior Department attorneys filed in federal court on 13 October to rescind the three-year-old federal operating approval for Revolution Wind, a 704 MW offshore wind farm off Connecticut and Rhode Island that has already begun delivering electricity to New England. Two prior stop-work orders were overturned by courts in 2025. The project is expected to reach full commercial output by end-2026. The legal action is the latest in a broader administration offshore wind rollback that has paused federal leases for five offshore projects, including Vineyard Wind, Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind, Sunrise Wind and Empire Wind. Developers Ørsted and Eversource have not publicly commented on the latest filing.

items.title: Liberty Mutual Re Parametric Earthquake Trigger Pays Out in Mexico; Sensor-Activated ILS Contract Demonstrates Rapid Claims Settlement for Climate-Linked Catastrophe Risk
items.body_html: A Liberty Mutual Re sensor-triggered earthquake insurance-linked security (ILS) contract paid out in Mexico in October 2026, according to Artemis.bm. The payout demonstrates the operational viability of parametric ILS structures — where settlement is triggered automatically by measured physical parameters (seismic intensity readings) rather than assessed loss, eliminating the settlement lag of traditional indemnity contracts. Parametric structures are gaining traction across earthquake, hurricane and flood perils as climate-driven event frequency increases pressure on conventional claims adjustment processes. The payout comes as the broader ILS market trades at a record outstanding of ~US$65.6 billion and as wildfire parametric products see accelerating investor interest alongside record cat bond issuance.
